vonnra.f_door.1.notes: After the accusation. The door listens 'as I am': she is admitting she has always been listening. Say the name as the answer she gives instead of yes. The last sentence is certainty, nearly affection, and a warning.

vonnra.f_door.2.wants: to keep the door closed and them curious
vonnra.f_door.2.notes: 'The door is not for sale' is flat finality. The last sentence is quiet prophecy; she is counting on them walking into it.

vonnra.cb_opened_vault.pace: slow and very controlled, a long pause after 'You opened it'
vonnra.cb_opened_vault.wants: to learn at once whether the living can pass
vonnra.cb_opened_vault.notes: The stillness is held by effort. 'I would rather you stood' means she wants to look at them whole, to see what the door did. The question is the only urgent thing she says in the game; keep it level, but let it come a fraction sooner.

vonnra.cb_vault2.pace: slow, the repeated 'that is all' slower still
vonnra.cb_vault2.wants: to close the subject before they ask more
vonnra.cb_vault2.notes: The Legion is still holding the door. Relief disguised as dismissal; the repetition is her steadying herself, not emphasis for them.

vonnra.cb_vault3.wants: to let them keep their silence, for a price
vonnra.cb_vault3.notes: 'It is. For now.' agrees without granting anything. 'You will find I collect' is soft and absolutely meant.

vonnra.cb_core_stolen.wants: to show she is still in control of what went wrong
vonnra.cb_core_stolen.notes: The heart was meant to stay at the ford. 'I am not angry' must sound true, and not quite be. 'I am arranging' is quiet steel.

vonnra.cb_exposed_pell.wants: to show the loss is only a ledger entry
vonnra.cb_exposed_pell.notes: Pell was one of her paid tongues. No resentment aloud; just a mind already moving to the next source.

vonnra.say_calling.1.pace: slow, a long pause before 'It is a lovely belief'
vonnra.say_calling.1.wants: to gently mock the idea of keeping things out
vonnra.say_calling.1.notes: She has spent her life keeping one thing in. The last sentence is almost fond, and quietly sad.

vonnra.say_calling.2.wants: to advise them to break with purpose
vonnra.say_calling.2.notes: Prophecy given as a dry piece of household advice. 'Try to choose them' is meant.

vonnra.say_calling.3.wants: to warn them off the people who collect such fires
vonnra.say_calling.3.notes: She knows where the fire came from; she paid for it. 'Some of them keep ledgers' is a real warning about the Vigil, and a small joke at her own expense.

vonnra.say_calling.4.wants: to let them know they were seen
vonnra.say_calling.4.notes: Unstartled. 'I noticed' is flat and quietly pleased, a point scored without a smile.

vonnra.say_calling.5.wants: to show that nothing reaches her window unobserved
vonnra.say_calling.5.notes: As the stalker line, for any other calling: unmoved, a little dry. 'I noticed' lands like a receipt.

vonnra.coin.pace: slow, a long pause before 'That was free'
vonnra.coin.wants: to speak of the coin without saying what it buys
vonnra.coin.notes: The single most personal thing she offers. 'Something that cannot be bought twice' is said with quiet resolve. Then the shutter comes down: 'Do not grow used to it' is crisp, almost embarrassed at having been generous.

vonnra.risen.pace: slow, pause after 'the first time', slower at the end
vonnra.risen.wants: to make sure they owe no one but her
vonnra.risen.notes: She is the one who holds the note, and nearly says so. 'Do not thank Chid' is sharp; the last clause should sound like a riddle and land like a claim.

vonnra.jessop.pace: slow, a long silence where she turns the page
vonnra.jessop.wants: to bury the question without lying outright
vonnra.jessop.notes: She sent him through the door. The pause is the page that did not need turning; then 'Clerks go south' is said with perfect calm, and 'the direction they fall in' carries a weight she will not explain.

vonnra.f_ember.1.pace: slow, a held pause before 'I wonder for what'
vonnra.f_ember.1.wants: to understand a move she did not arrange
vonnra.f_ember.1.notes: Genuine curiosity, rare for her. 'I wonder for what' is the only open question she lets herself ask, and she half suspects the answer.

vonnra.f_ember.2.pace: slow, careful separation of the last two sentences
vonnra.f_ember.2.wants: to teach them the difference between honest and good
vonnra.f_ember.2.notes: No warmth in 'That is honest'. Let the full stop sit before 'It is not the same thing as good'; she knows that difference from the inside.

vonnra.f_ember.4.wants: to note an end everyone heard
vonnra.f_ember.4.notes: No 'I see' here: everyone saw it. A touch of irony in 'Everyone did'.

vonnra.f_ember.6.wants: to warn that the trade will finish itself
vonnra.f_ember.6.notes: 'Someone always does' is a law she lives by. Neither threat nor regret; a ledger fact.

vonnra.f_ember.7.wants: to plant a question they have not asked
vonnra.f_ember.7.notes: She knows what B.E. means and lets the letters hang unread. 'Someone always does' is quiet and certain.

vonnra.f_past.1.wants: to prove she sees what she has paid to hear
vonnra.f_past.1.notes: She is not looking at the palm: this is pillow talk bought from Sella, recited as vision. Let it sound like memory more than seeing; a soft, almost tender image of the child with the bow.

vonnra.f_past.2.pace: slow, inward, a dry weight on 'not meant to'
vonnra.f_past.2.wants: to show she knows their secrets
vonnra.f_past.2.notes: Recited, not read: her eyes are on their face. The stolen lens is a small knife she lays on the table, quietly pleased.

vonnra.f_past.3.wants: to let them know their past is no longer private
vonnra.f_past.3.notes: Bought talk, said as sight. 'The trick of walking away from it' has a hint of respect from someone who walks away from nothing.

vonnra.f_past.4.wants: to touch the one thing in their past she understands
vonnra.f_past.4.notes: Lamps nobody came to see: she knows about lighting lamps for her own reasons. Bought words, but the warmth that slips into 'lighting them anyway' is her own.

vonnra.f_past.5.wants: to admit nothing about what she does not know
vonnra.f_past.5.notes: Nobody sold her this one, so she makes the gap sound like the river's doing. 'Most do' is calm, a little rueful.

vonnra.f_accuse.pace: extremely slow, a very long silence before speaking
vonnra.f_accuse.wants: to keep them in the chair now the truth is close
vonnra.f_accuse.notes: For the first time she looks at their face. Everything is in the silence before the words. The name is her only answer, said quietly, almost gently; 'I have not finished reading' is a plea dressed as an order.

keegan.first.pace: projected, crisp, a quick defensive tag
keegan.first.wants: to be taken seriously at her post
keegan.first.notes: Full lecturer's projection on 'Halt!'. Tiny wince before 'Probationary', then 'It is a real title' rushed out, sincere and wounded in advance.

keegan.hub.1.wants: to tease them into reading something
keegan.hub.1.notes: A tutor's affectionate scolding. Answer her own question with relish; 'I can tell' is pleased with itself.

keegan.hub.2.wants: to keep a judgement she is not sure of
keegan.hub.2.notes: 'I would know' should sound confident; underneath, she has started looking for the signs and hopes she never finds them.

keegan.north.notes: Recited from the handbook. Weight on 'chapter four', said a fraction too carefully, as if it were hot to touch.

keegan.ch4.pace: short, stiff, a beat before 'chapter four'
keegan.ch4.wants: to close the subject at once
keegan.ch4.notes: She knows what chapter four is about and is afraid it is about the person in front of her. Clipped, no joke in it.

keegan.prof.pace: lecturing, lively, a quick slip at the end
keegan.prof.wants: to show off a little and laugh at herself
keegan.prof.notes: Light comic story. Teacherly pleasure naming 'litotes'; 'You're welcome' comes out with a contraction because she is enjoying herself and forgets.

keegan.warden.pace: quick at first, then lowered, careful
keegan.warden.wants: to warn them while not breaking rank
keegan.warden.notes: '...Who told you that?' is genuinely startled, the projection dropping. The history is half-whispered lecture. 'Do not repeat that. I am probationary.' is anxious, as if her superiors might hear.

keegan.who.wants: to test what they really saw
keegan.who.notes: She is beginning to wonder about them. 'You were there' is a probe dressed as a debating point.

keegan.ashe.wants: to explain her duty by his example
keegan.ashe.notes: The one figure she venerates. Warmth and gravity, less performance. 'Once you were ready' is careful; she is measuring them as she says it.

keegan.vigil.pace: brisk start, then slowing and smaller
keegan.vigil.wants: to believe the Vigil is still there
keegan.vigil.notes: Bright and dutiful to 'They are very busy'. After the pause the lecture voice falters; 'being read by nobody' is small and lonely. She never admits the Vigil is gone.

keegan.ready.wants: to warn them without frightening them
keegan.ready.notes: The real fear surfaces in 'You would not like it if I saw them'. Then she scrambles; 'the paperwork' is a lame joke she clings to.

keegan.cb_opened_vault.wants: to scold them with the full force of the handbook
keegan.cb_opened_vault.notes: Proper lecture delivery; land 'don't, in several sizes' as a deadpan punchline. Real worry under the joke.

keegan.cb_core_stolen.wants: to do something, anything, by the book
keegan.cb_core_stolen.notes: The pause after 'the ford' is real fright. Then the fragments are comic escalation; 'In capitals' is said with grim determination.

keegan.say_calling.1.notes: Delighted, then deflated. The last line is prim but affectionate, a lecturer's gossip about a rude chapter.

keegan.say_calling.2.wants: to keep the big weapon away from her gate
keegan.say_calling.2.notes: Overly correct courtesy masking alarm. 'Considerably less forgiving' is a dry, pedantic little flourish.

keegan.say_calling.3.wants: to hide what the Vigil wrote about such people
keegan.say_calling.3.notes: She nearly cites the ledger of the Unchained and catches herself. The 'Good morning' is far too bright; 'is it not' is a nervous non-question.

keegan.say_calling.4.pace: brisk, then a small confession after the pause
keegan.say_calling.4.wants: to save face and then be honest
keegan.say_calling.4.notes: Fake confidence through 'merely being polite'; the pause, then 'I did not know' is small and endearing.

keegan.say_calling.5.notes: Same text as the stalker line, for any other calling: crisp bluff, then the honest climb-down, quieter.

keegan.dinner.pace: rapid, self-interrupting, a final clipped exit
keegan.dinner.wants: to say yes without saying it
keegan.dinner.notes: The lecture voice collapses into honesty. 'I have read it four times' should be a mortified rush; 'very nearly no' is soft and hopeful; 'Good day' is a hasty retreat.

keegan.t_keegan.pace: slower, softer, then brisk on the bath
keegan.t_keegan.wants: to be recognised as what she believes she is
keegan.t_keegan.notes: Real longing on 'without the bracket'; let it sit. Then the bath line breaks the spell with prim, comic indignation.

keegan.say_risen.wants: to get away before she has to name what she sees
keegan.say_risen.notes: She knows chapter four's signs and has just seen one. The long look happens in the pause. 'You look extremely well' is too careful. Contractions slip on 'I've got to go': the tell. The stammered repeat is panic barely held.

board.read.1.notes: Read like a sign: stress BOUNTY and the numbers; signature dropped off at the end, flatter still.

board.read.2.pace: even, small beat before the graffiti
board.read.2.wants: to let the town's confusion show through the order
board.read.2.notes: Hit SUSPENDED as the sign-writer meant it. Drop to a drier, almost amused aside for 'why??', as if reading someone's pencil.

board.read.3.wants: to mark the end of the trouble with a shrug
board.read.3.notes: WITHDRAWN in capitals, 'The stream runs clear' plain. The underneath 'about time' dry and low.

board.read.4.wants: to close a chapter on the board
board.read.4.notes: Official and slightly stiff; the thanks is clerical, not heartfelt.

board.read.5.wants: to let the town's suspicion of the player show in an order
board.read.5.notes: Press WALK WITH PEOPLE as the sign-writer's emphasis; the rest flat. No knowing tone.

board.read.6.pace: steady, a beat before the third sentence
board.read.6.wants: to let one plain line carry a death
board.read.6.notes: CURFEW stressed; 'One of ours did not come home.' read with no extra weight, which is the weight.

board.read.7.wants: to let a stranger's grief slip in under the notice
board.read.7.notes: AT REST read as a heading, the details plain. Drop for 'he hummed', drier and quieter, a different hand.

board.read.8.wants: to lay the missing caravan before the player
board.read.8.notes: MISSING and REWARD stressed as the capitals ask; initials clipped.

board.read.9.wants: to give the player the town's thanks at arm's length
board.read.9.notes: THANK YOU leads; keep the rest read, not felt. 'Jory is home' gets the barest give.

board.read.10.wants: to let an absence say what happened
board.read.10.notes: Not a notice but what you see: say it low and plain, a beat on 'Only the nail is left.'

board.read.11.notes: BY ORDER OF THE WATCH read like a stamp; the rest flat legalese.

board.read.12.wants: to post the hunt with a sting in the tail
board.read.12.notes: WANTED stressed. The last sentence is the sign-writer's own jab: say it drier, almost deadpan.

board.read.13.wants: to tell the player they are being looked for
board.read.13.notes: WANTED stressed, then deadpan on 'but not poor enough'. No wink.

board.read.14.wants: to plant the tremor as a question
board.read.14.notes: Scrawled, not a notice: read it as a scribble, low and a little uncertain; initial dropped flat.

board.read.15.wants: to let the graffiti say what the notice hides
board.read.15.notes: Notice voice for CARTERS WANTED and DOUBLE; then drier for the pencil line; then flatter again for 'Wat went. Wat's not back.' Let it sit.

board.read.16.notes: Short and practical; WANTED as heading, the name dropped off.

board.read.17.wants: to give the player a breath of ordinary life
board.read.17.notes: Read straight; 'Answers to nothing.' dry and level, not cute.

board.read.18.wants: to close a small story kindly
board.read.18.notes: Plain and a little sheepish, as written. No punchline.

sella.first.1.wants: to make the town's new hero a customer
sella.first.1.notes: Low and amused, a laugh behind 'big dead bastard'. She is sizing up a valuable talker as well as a client. The last two short lines are her sign on the door: plain, friendly, not coy.

sella.first.2.wants: to offer comfort at a price
sella.first.2.notes: Warm opener with 'love', meant and also a pitch. Unhurried; 'The rest isn't' is matter-of-fact, never breathy.

sella.hub.1.notes: The repetition is a running joke she enjoys; each 'asking' a shade more knowing. Adult, amused, unhurried, not breathy.

sella.hub.2.wants: to make the regular feel welcome
sella.hub.2.notes: Casual banter; the business line is honest, which is the joke.

sella.again.1.pace: light tease, then a dry jab
sella.again.1.notes: Mock-hurt; 'You'd have been robbed' is professional pride, smiled.

sella.again.2.notes: A bawdy compliment to herself, deadpan. Warmth and work at once.

sella.hear.1.notes: She is selling this, and she knows it; the clerk anecdote is told with comic contempt ('Charming'). After the pause, the Tuesday-man detail carries genuine unease: Jessop never misses.

sella.hear.2.notes: Easy gossip, nothing dear; 'Same as ever' with a little yawn. Harlan's tears are said kindly.

sella.hear.3.pace: brisk list, a darker note, flat finish
sella.hear.3.wants: to give the survivor the town's mood
sella.hear.3.notes: Bawdy insult for Holloway with a grin, then the north road line lands colder; she has lost customers that way. Back to flat for 'Same as ever'.

sella.rook.wants: to defend Rook without going soft
sella.rook.notes: Laughs at the Kerchief through the door. 'I've had worse mothers' is the line that slips: delivered as a joke, it isn't one. Don't dwell.

sella.buyers.pace: brisk list, pause, then slower and pointed
sella.buyers.wants: to be honest about the trade without pricing herself out
sella.buyers.notes: Says 'Clever' with respect. The list is plain business; Vonnra's name gets the most weight. After the pause it turns personal: 'Nobody has. Yet.' is a warning and a confession, half-smiled.

sella.price.notes: A price list said with warmth and no coyness. The last two sentences are consent, practical and kind, the voice of someone who does this well. Adult, steady, never breathy.

sella.night.1.wants: to hold the place of a scene not yet written
sella.night.1.notes: Writer's placeholder, not for recording; any guide take is flat and neutral.

sella.night.2.pace: unhurried, then brisk at the end
sella.night.2.wants: to give the night its warmth and then its bill
sella.night.2.notes: Frank, never coy or breathy. A little lift on 'laughs at the last one'; land 'She is dressed, and counting.' dry and level.

sella.morning.1.notes: Tenderness at the edges and quickly put away: 'I don't mind' is more than she means to give, so she hides behind Rook and the joke about killing.

sella.morning.2.wants: to send them off without admitting she cares
sella.morning.2.notes: Morning-after banter, frank and funny. 'The pieces are what I like' is bawdy and also a real wish for them to come back alive.

sella.cb_tricked_redcowl.notes: Professional respect for a good lie; a wink on 'upstairs'.

sella.cb_exposed_pell.wants: to note the cost to business
sella.cb_exposed_pell.notes: Cheerful contempt; she means the money part and nothing else.

sella.cb_burned_roost.pace: report, pause, careful words, then plain
sella.cb_burned_roost.wants: to let them know she knows
sella.cb_burned_roost.notes: The pause is her choosing not to judge. 'It's bad for business' is her armour; 'But I heard' is flat and serious. She will also sell it.

sella.cb_freed_teamsters.pace: storytelling, a laugh, then gentle advice
sella.cb_freed_teamsters.notes: Delighted by Jory blushing; warmth for him is real. 'He thinks you're a story' is soft, almost protective.

sella.say_calling.1.pace: slow appraisal, then a quick quip
sella.say_calling.1.notes: Unhurried look at the armour; the buckle line is a practised joke she still enjoys.

sella.say_calling.2.notes: Admiring and practical; the furniture line is a real house rule said with a smile.

sella.say_calling.3.notes: Light comic build; the last sentence is half a joke and half genuinely unnerved by the heat.

sella.say_calling.4.wants: to set a boundary with a joke
sella.say_calling.4.notes: Recovered from the start before she speaks; the candlestick is a real threat dressed as banter.

sella.say_calling.5.wants: to warn without losing the customer
sella.say_calling.5.notes: A little jump in the first sentence, then easy humour. The rule about creeping up on her is meant.

sella.say_woman.wants: to put a woman client at ease
sella.say_woman.notes: Frank and kind; no coyness. The last line is wry about loneliness, hers included.

sella.say_maeca.notes: Savour the repeated 'Maeca. Humming.' with disbelief. The competition line is a joke with a sliver of something else under it.

sella.t_sella.wants: to be wanted as a person, not a trade
sella.t_sella.notes: The one time the work drops. Say the house plainly; 'somebody who knocks' is the whole wish, and the repeat is quieter. Not pitiful, not sentimental.

sella.free.pace: firm, pause, then a little brittle
sella.free.wants: to give without it becoming a thing
sella.free.notes: Not working tonight, and it scares her. The pause is her watching their face; the last two short lines guard against being seen. Low, adult, not breathy.

sella.free_night.1.wants: to hold the place of a scene not yet written
sella.free_night.1.notes: Writer's placeholder, not for recording; any guide take is flat and neutral.

sella.free_night.2.wants: to let the player notice what is different this time
sella.free_night.2.notes: Quieter than her paid night. Weight the bolt 'which she has never done' lightly; let 'and then she sleeps' trail into silence.

sella.free_morning.pace: light joke, pause, then slow and serious
sella.free_morning.wants: to protect the survivor from what she sells
sella.free_morning.notes: She is still there, which she never is. The Rook joke is cover. After the pause, the Vonnra warning is the nearest she comes to confessing; 'I mean that kindly' is quiet and true.

sella.past.1.notes: She listens properly and enjoys the picture of them young. 'I'd have guessed, but not that' is warm and slightly puzzled. What is said here may be sold, and she knows it.

sella.past.2.notes: A gentle tease ('cloister rat'), then 'Good for you, love' warmly meant: she knows about getting out.

sella.past.3.pace: dry, a low laugh, then conspiratorial
sella.past.3.notes: The pause is her low laugh. 'Takes one to know one' hints at her own past, unexplained. 'Don't tell Rook' is a shared joke.

sella.past.4.wants: to honour what they told her
sella.past.4.notes: She is quiet a moment before the second sentence. 'Saddest thing' is said without performance; the last clause keeps it from tipping into pity.

sella.sleeptalk.wants: to tell them without frightening them
sella.sleeptalk.notes: The image is gently told; she was awake listening. The shrug is a pause; 'I don't think you did either' is kind and a little uneasy. Whatever she caught, she may still sell.

greymuzzle.first.wants: to make the player hold still with the old wolf
greymuzzle.first.notes: Each sentence one look. No menace in the voice; the last line about the wolves that do not get up is said plainly, and is the worst of it.

greymuzzle.show.wants: to show the sickness and the ask without saying either
greymuzzle.show.notes: Black gums and milky eyes said as plain fact. A small pause after 'and cannot'. 'and waits' is left open.

greymuzzle.ally.pace: measured, a held beat before the end
greymuzzle.ally.wants: to let the old wolf's sacrifice register
greymuzzle.ally.notes: The howl line gets a little air after it. 'He is not coming. They are his answer.' low and certain, no swell.

greymuzzle.again.1.wants: to let the player feel accepted, wordlessly
greymuzzle.again.1.notes: Gentle and brief; a wolf turning its back is trust, so let it rest, not land.

greymuzzle.again.2.wants: to let the missing wolves be counted by the player
greymuzzle.again.2.notes: Say 'are not there any more' without weight; the absence does the work. Cool on the weather image.

greymuzzle.again.3.wants: to give the player a wolf's thanks
greymuzzle.again.3.notes: A hint of warmth on 'as good as thanks', no more. Nothing sentimental.

greymuzzle.again.4.notes: Two flat sentences. Leave the space after them.

redcowl.first.1.wants: to make the killer of his people account for it
redcowl.first.1.notes: The only greeting without a laugh: every crossbow is up and he means it. Big chest voice held down low. 'Talk, and talk slow' is an order with a grave in it.

redcowl.first.2.wants: to find out whose side the stranger is on
redcowl.first.2.notes: Eyes the red colours with half a grin; a dig at Holloway's men. The last word, 'Talk', drops cold.

redcowl.first.3.pace: brisk, a laugh in the middle, hard close
redcowl.first.3.wants: to keep a mage from burning the camp
redcowl.first.3.notes: The tent story is half a laugh at himself; the instruction is not. Leans on 'cold'.

redcowl.first.4.wants: to recruit or intimidate, whichever works
redcowl.first.4.notes: Laughs before he threatens: 'Ha!' full-chested and genuine. 'Don't make me find out which dozen' drops cold on the turn.

redcowl.first.5.wants: to keep the peace in his camp
redcowl.first.5.notes: Crude humour about his lads, but the point is that she is safe because he has ordered it; say 'where I've told them' with authority. Then curt.

redcowl.first.6.wants: to decide whether to like or kill the stranger
redcowl.first.6.notes: Easy and amused; the question is real and the answer decides things. A hint of steel on 'Which is it?'

redcowl.hub.notes: A grunt of a laugh; he's warming to them and won't show it.

redcowl.who.pace: proud, then bitter, pause, laugh, then curt
redcowl.who.wants: to make the stranger see his people
redcowl.who.notes: 'Mine' is fatherly and fierce. 'Forty-one mouths' is the number he lives by. The Watch line is bitter: he nearly says Ashford and doesn't. The pause and 'Ha! Listen to me' is him catching himself; the turn back to threat is covering.

redcowl.rav.pace: big laugh, then quick and warmer
redcowl.rav.notes: 'Ha! HA.' full and real; the 'old saw-bones' is a brother's affection he will never name. Generous, then a joke-threat to keep face.

redcowl.goods.notes: Plain terms; salvage is how forty-one mouths eat. The teamsters line is a grumble about rations, not cruelty.

redcowl.deal.pace: brisk, then a pause and a low warning
redcowl.deal.notes: Pleased with the gold; 'my lads won't stop you' is a guarantee. The pause after 'And' marks the turn to cold: the Holloway line is a real warning, low and level.
redcowl.deal.say: Pleasure. Box is by the tents; the teamsters are in the cages. Open them yourself; my lads won't stop you. And if Holloway asks, you've never seen my face.

redcowl.favour.wants: to repay a favour without looking soft
redcowl.favour.notes: 'Is it, now' is doubtful. The howling admission is weary. Pause, then 'Fine' and the bargain; 'Fifty, for a friend' is a gruff kindness he would deny.

redcowl.prisoners.wants: to recover the cost of feeding them
redcowl.prisoners.notes: Mild irritation at the praying; the fifty is for food, meant literally.

redcowl.released.notes: Casual directions; 'he bites' is a dry joke with a grain of truth.

redcowl.pell.pace: reads, quickens, explodes, cuts off, then cold resolve
redcowl.pell.notes: Reads the ledger aloud, slowing on 'after'. 'After!' is a roar of betrayal. The insult is cut off. Then very cold and fast: the turn to murder is quiet.

redcowl.trick.pace: dismissive, breaks off, then roaring commands
redcowl.trick.notes: Starts contemptuous of the Watch's numbers; the dash is the whistle from the ridge. Then full-chest shouting orders, two repeats, urgent but in control: a chief, not a coward.

redcowl.cages.1.wants: to be seen as more than a bandit
redcowl.cages.1.notes: Explains with hard logic and a gravedigger's weariness on 'worth-nothings'. Pause; 'And I feed them' is his pride and the point; 'before I feed my own' is fierce and quiet.

redcowl.cages.2.wants: to justify the cages on his own terms
redcowl.cages.2.notes: Not a laugh in it. 'I've buried enough' is Ashford, unsaid. After the pause, the feeding line is the man underneath: insist on it, almost angry to be doubted.

redcowl.wagons.notes: Laughs at the painted wagons; 'The road knows now' is relish. The last line is sly: he knows the wagons hold something worth wanting.

redcowl.crates.wants: to dodge what's in the crates
redcowl.crates.notes: A camp tale told for laughs, with a real shiver in 'listened to it think about it'. He doesn't know what B.E. is; he does know it is dangerous.

redcowl.crates_dig.pace: no laugh, slow, distant, then urgent
redcowl.crates_dig.wants: to know how close the danger is
redcowl.crates_dig.notes: He does not laugh. He looks north-east, at the hill; the pause is that look. 'The one that's been knocking' is low and private: Ashford went into the ground. The question is the first he really needs answered.

redcowl.crates_keep.pace: hard list, firm, then a rueful half-laugh
redcowl.crates_keep.wants: to keep the ember from everyone
redcowl.crates_keep.notes: Each 'Not' is a door slammed. 'They stay with me' is final. The pause is a small laugh, not the big one; the mother line is the family reach under strain, rueful and private.

redcowl.crates_charge.pace: long silence, then clipped, then cold
redcowl.crates_charge.wants: to strike the Dig through the survivor
redcowl.crates_charge.notes: A long look before speaking (the lad carries the crate like a sleeping baby). Instructions low and deliberate; the pause before 'run' is the turn: the last word cold and urgent.
redcowl.crates_charge.say: Take it. Put it where it'll do the most harm to the right people. And then... run.

redcowl.birds.1.pace: big laugh, fond description, stop, flat warning
redcowl.birds.1.notes: The bird is his brother, unnamed; the description is fond despite himself. The laugh stops dead at the pause. 'Not in my camp' is cold and final.

redcowl.birds.2.notes: Warm, amused about the drinking seamster; he is protecting his brother. Where the laugh stops, go cold and quiet: 'Birds don't have names' is a threat.

redcowl.ashford.pace: laugh dies, one word, silence, quiet and final
redcowl.ashford.wants: to never hear that name again
redcowl.ashford.notes: The laugh goes out like a lamp. 'Don't.' alone. Then quiet, very still: the threat lives in how soft it is. Under it is the whole buried town.

redcowl.pell_given.pace: short laugh, then quick and urgent
redcowl.pell_given.notes: Laugh first, then the threat. He's already shouting for boots; the last lines are an order and also care for the survivor, said cold.

redcowl.pell_hunt.notes: No laugh. Low and deliberate; 'a smell of ink' with contempt.

snib.first.2.wants: to stop the intruder and look important
snib.first.2.notes: Big shout on 'OI!', a lamp-ring on the stressed words. Then the self-introduction is proud and small. 'It does, actually' is the contradiction gag: a sudden honest deflation before 'But quick'.

snib.hub.3.wants: to show nothing has changed and he is in charge
snib.hub.3.notes: Weary self-important routine, two status reports.

snib.ember.wants: to protect himself while telling everything
snib.ember.notes: He denies knowing, then lists it all in order, unable to stop. The 'man with soft hands and a big book' is pure observation. 'Snib did not say any of this' is whispered panic.

snib.poison.wants: to justify the pump without guilt
snib.poison.notes: Reciting the Boss's orders with fervour; 'the heart wants DOWN' is the Boss's voice coming out of him. The wolves line is dismissive and petty.

snib.move.wants: to take credit for the idea
snib.move.notes: Thinking aloud through 'Deeper is good'; the change to 'Fine! FINE.' is sudden. 'Snib has had an idea!' is proud, theft in plain sight.

snib.lamp.wants: to obey the Boss and not be blamed
snib.lamp.notes: Shock and awe at the spare lamp; 'SPIT' is absurd emphasis. Then the frantic not-seeing and barked orders to the lads.

snib.bribe.wants: to strike a deal and keep deniability
snib.bribe.notes: Calculating, pleased with himself. The last two sentences are an innocent shrug that fools nobody.

snib.bribed.wants: to act out the 'accident' for anyone listening
snib.bribed.notes: Hammed-up sorrow, badly acted; 'SO sad' the worst of it, with a grin underneath.

snib.pipelads.pace: quick, flat, cracking on the last lines
snib.pipelads.wants: to stop thinking about what he escaped
snib.pipelads.notes: Rattled off like a list he has heard too often. 'Snib got promoted' is quiet and nearly ashamed; then the panic and the shove on 'LEAVE'. The one moment Snib is not funny.

snib.what.pace: quick, chatty, a sudden snap at the end
snib.what.wants: to look knowledgeable and avoid thinking
snib.what.notes: Enthusiastic about the stream, 'obliging' said fondly. After the pause, 'Snib has never needed to KNOW' is defensive, a little too loud.

survivor.first.wants: to make sense of what it saw
survivor.first.notes: Dry, close whisper. 'MOVED' is a sudden hoarse stress, then back down. The three Grimtunnel lines are said like a lesson learnt by rote, each the same shape, each more afraid.

survivor.what.pace: whispered, stopping and starting, rushing at the end
survivor.what.wants: to be rid of the map and the knowledge
survivor.what.notes: The repeated 'Still lit' is the horror: the lamp came back, Kell did not. 'There is always another' is flat, certain. The last sentence rushes, pressing the map on them, desperate to forget.

jory.first.pace: halting, then the story spills out fast
jory.first.wants: to make someone believe what happened
jory.first.notes: Seventeen and shaken. The dash is him not knowing how to thank someone for that. A small awkward smile on Uncle crying. Then the account rushes out in order, as if rehearsed in the dark; 'And they were waiting' drops quiet.

jory.hub.1.wants: to be left alone about it
jory.hub.1.notes: 'I'm all right' is a lie said too fast. Pause. The line about Uncle is dull and knowing: he knows the crates were never salt.

jory.hub.2.notes: Teenage weariness over fear; a tiny huff on 'Uncle keeps asking', fond and fed up.

jory.crates.pace: listing, a small laugh, pause, then a real question
jory.crates.notes: Easy recital until 'every rut in Thornhollow', said with a boy's bravado. The pause is the doubt arriving; the question is quiet and young.

jory.truth.pace: a single laugh, repeating, pause, then very small
jory.truth.notes: The laugh happens before speaking. Repeat the rut line as if it were funny, then the laugh drains out at the pause. 'Uncle knew' is barely voiced; 'He told me salt' is a child's hurt.

jory.truth_knew.pace: slow repeated nods, pause, then shaky
jory.truth_knew.notes: He keeps nodding; 'Right. Right.' is automatic. The thanks is Harlan's own phrase coming out of him: the family under stress. A queasy, not-quite laugh on 'I think'.

jory.truth_ask.wants: to be brave enough to confront Uncle
jory.truth_ask.notes: He says it and doesn't move. The second 'I will' is weaker, persuading himself.

jory.salt.notes: The light goes out of his face like a child's. He accepts the lie because he wants to; 'Thanks' is small and a little lost.

wayfinder.first.notes: Quick read of them, approving 'Good.'. Relish in listing the places like entries in a catalogue. 'Won't want you there' is cheerful gallows humour.

wayfinder.hub.1.wants: to welcome back a good customer
wayfinder.hub.1.notes: Pleased they lived, and pleased for the ledger. A quick turn to business on 'I've new ones'.

wayfinder.hub.2.wants: to get them looking at the maps
wayfinder.hub.2.notes: Short shopkeeper patter; friendly but already turning back to her pen.

wayfinder.oaths.wants: to make sure they take the oaths seriously
wayfinder.oaths.notes: A cartographer's precision on the list. The last two sentences are deadpan gallows humour; let 'Those are the choices' land flat.

wayfinder.places.wants: to give them the rules of survival
wayfinder.places.notes: Laid out like map directions. 'Some do. I sell them fewer maps.' is dry: those who stay do not come back to buy.

wayfinder.drawn.pace: steady, a slight hush at the end
wayfinder.drawn.wants: to explain her trade without giving away the buyer
wayfinder.drawn.notes: 'I buy what they remember' is plain commerce. 'Where their light went out' softens into something nearly reverent; she has looked for one light in particular.

wayfinder.notes.pace: breezy list, then a slower aside
wayfinder.notes.notes: The list of buyers is vague and fast; 'silver ink' is a fraction too specific. After the pause, 'So has he' slips out as guilt and warning both. She sells their name and half wants them to know.

wayfinder.cb_nemesis_slain.wants: to note a story worth recording
wayfinder.cb_nemesis_slain.notes: Genuinely impressed. 'People like reading about that' has an edge: one reader in particular.

wayfinder.cb_opened_vault.wants: to keep the stair off her pages
wayfinder.cb_opened_vault.notes: A joke covering a real line she will not cross. 'I don't draw that far down' is said a little too fast.

wayfinder.say_calling.1.wants: to give them a useful warning
wayfinder.say_calling.1.notes: Practical respect, then a wry caution about holding on too long; she knows something about that.

wayfinder.say_calling.2.wants: to tell them she would rather they lived
wayfinder.say_calling.2.notes: Breezy, but 'but I do' is meant. The last joke is about trade; under it, she has a stake in who comes back.

wayfinder.say_calling.3.pace: brisk, a beat before the last line
wayfinder.say_calling.3.notes: 'Brighter and faster' is professional appraisal. 'I've a margin for people like you' has a collector's gleam she would not want them to examine.

wayfinder.say_calling.4.wants: to steer them to the right ground
wayfinder.say_calling.4.notes: Pointing at the map on 'Here, and here'. The reaver jibe is a quick aside, affectionate.

wayfinder.say_calling.5.wants: to sell them the right map
wayfinder.say_calling.5.notes: As the stalker line, for any other calling: crisp advice, a light joke at the reavers' expense.

wayfinder.t_wayfinder.pace: slower, clipped, a long pause before 'My brother didn't'
wayfinder.t_wayfinder.wants: to answer without telling the truth
wayfinder.t_wayfinder.notes: 'My brother didn't' is the lie she has told for twelve years; say it as if it were simply true. The joke about the corners is how she keeps it bearable, and the crack shows.

wayfinder.margin.pace: brisk list, a beat where she dips the pen
wayfinder.margin.wants: to get their name into the book
wayfinder.margin.notes: Light, tidy, practised. 'How do I put you down?' sounds like a clerk's formality; it is the sale.

wayfinder.margin_name.pace: slow and deliberate, a pause while she blots
wayfinder.margin_name.wants: to fix them in the record
wayfinder.margin_name.notes: Satisfaction in a neat entry. 'For good' carries more than she says: the name will go north.

wayfinder.margin_nobody.wants: to humour them and keep the record
wayfinder.margin_nobody.notes: She writes it straight. 'More than most' is wry; she knows exactly which kind of Nobody comes back.

wayfinder.margin_lark.wants: to name them on her own terms
wayfinder.margin_lark.notes: A considering look, then decision. The lark joke is affectionate teasing; she is quietly making them harder to trace.

bark.rook.2.notes: An order flung over her shoulder.

bark.rook.3.notes: A joke with no smile; she'd still patch you up.

bark.rook.4.pace: brisk, beat before the second half
bark.rook.4.notes: A practised line; the second half gets a laugh on the out-breath.

bark.rook.night.1.notes: Her rule and her mother's lamp behind it; quiet, almost a vow.

bark.rook.night.2.notes: Kind first, then the dry bad news.

bark.rook.night.4.pace: low, dry, building to the joke
bark.rook.night.4.notes: A bawdy aside with a straight face; 'and nothing else' with the out-breath laugh.

bark.holloway.1.notes: A muster-sergeant call, said too many times.

bark.holloway.2.notes: A routine order; no aggression, just watchfulness.

bark.holloway.3.notes: The second 'Three.' is quieter and heavier: a tally, not a complaint.

bark.holloway.night.2.notes: Counts his men out loud; the last line is a quiet admission to himself.

bark.holloway.night.3.notes: Hoarse, almost gentle; the end of a long shift.

bark.holloway.night.4.pace: slow, low, a beat before 'Go home'
bark.holloway.night.4.wants: to keep one more son alive
bark.holloway.night.4.notes: Said plainly, no self-pity. 'Go home' is a plea dressed as an order.

bark.holloway.night.5.notes: A soldier's superstition; quiet and tense.

bark.maeca.1.notes: Half to herself; the second sentence lands heavier.

bark.maeca.2.notes: Said like weather. The hunter's half-voice, eyes on the trees.

bark.maeca.3.notes: Not friendly, not unfriendly; a fact a hunter gives once.

bark.maeca.night.1.wants: to make you hear the silence
bark.maeca.night.1.notes: A question, a listening silence, 'No.' The worry is in the stillness; keep the voice down.

bark.maeca.night.2.notes: To herself, over Rav's ale. Weary, not drunk.

bark.maeca.night.3.notes: Not frightened; reading the noise. A slight tightening at the end.

bark.maeca.night.4.wants: to make someone listen to him
bark.maeca.night.4.notes: Greymuzzle is sick and she loves him and won't say so. 'Listen.' is barely there; let the care show only in the softness.

bark.chid.1.wants: to keep the shrine's story alive
bark.chid.1.notes: Said to nobody, as a habit. A small smile on 'you know'.

bark.chid.2.notes: A man talking himself through another day. Gentle, self-mocking turn on the second sentence.

bark.chid.3.pace: unhurried, a beat before 'I should know'
bark.chid.3.notes: 'I should know' is far older than he looks and he does not notice; keep it light, not ominous.

bark.chid.night.1.notes: Murmured like a bedtime prayer. Warm, never preachy.

bark.chid.night.2.wants: to leave a light for the lost
bark.chid.night.2.notes: Matter-of-fact kindness. 'Somebody' might be someone long dead; don't lean on it.

bark.chid.night.3.notes: A small warm aside, as if he has met many night-walkers like this.

bark.chid.night.4.pace: recited, then a slower wry aside
bark.chid.night.4.wants: to hold on to the old words a little longer
bark.chid.night.4.notes: The Order's saying comes out word-perfect from long use. Pause, then the aside about tonight is weary humour, not doubt.

bark.rav.1.notes: Mock-threat with a grin under it.

bark.rav.2.notes: A half-sigh; the habit is his brother, unspoken.

bark.rav.4.wants: to get on with the job
bark.rav.4.notes: Doctor's frankness, completely unembarrassed; deadpan on the leeches.

bark.rav.5.notes: Grim joke, flat delivery, a ghost of a laugh.

bark.rav.6.notes: A tavern pitch with music in it; the broken heart gets a softer drink.

bark.rav.night.1.wants: to joke about the late hour
bark.rav.night.1.notes: Half-drunk drawl; the second sentence a leer, amused at himself.

bark.rav.night.2.wants: to get the survivor to stay
bark.rav.night.2.notes: Inviting; already past the third cup.

bark.rav.night.3.notes: Warm invitation, then the blood line dry and unbothered.

bark.rav.night.4.notes: Slurring a little; pleased with his own joke.

bark.harlan.1.notes: Muttered; the second sentence a stubborn insistence that cracks a little on the name.

bark.harlan.2.notes: A market cry with nothing behind it; 'when the wagons come' is the hope he is selling himself.

bark.harlan.3.notes: Said to no one, a little resentful at the whole town.

bark.harlan.night.1.notes: Soft, tired, nearly confiding. 'Helps me not think' is a small honest admission.

bark.harlan.night.2.notes: Half a whisper, eyes on the dark road; the grief sounds almost like hope.

bark.harlan.night.3.pace: two clipped words, pause, one word
bark.harlan.night.3.wants: to stay awake for the boy

bark.harlan.night.4.pace: repeat with a catch, then soft
bark.harlan.night.4.notes: The second 'Hated it' nearly a laugh; the candle detail is fond and hurts, because Jory is out in the dark.

bark.pell.1.notes: Murmured, half a joke; smile on 'two'.

bark.pell.2.notes: Practised condolence for the street; a trace of satisfaction under it.

bark.pell.3.notes: A courteous notice spoken aloud; firmer than it needs to be.

bark.pell.night.1.wants: to be left alone in the dark
bark.pell.night.1.notes: The second 'Closed!' nearly loses control; 'Come back in daylight' is him reaching for manners.

bark.pell.night.2.notes: Grumbled to himself, fussy and tired.

bark.pell.night.3.wants: to know who is in the dark
bark.pell.night.3.notes: Quick and a little high; he is frightened, so it is clipped and careful rather than loud.

bark.pell.night.4.notes: Tired and half-amused; the numbers he means are the ones in the hill.

bark.wenna.1.notes: Muttered to herself; the repeat 'Never' is stubborn and a bit scared, which she'd deny.

bark.wenna.2.notes: A grumbling refrain to herself as she sorts. Light.

bark.wenna.3.notes: To herself, sniffing. A herbalist's worry, not a complaint.

bark.wenna.night.3.pace: brisk, beat before the second half
bark.wenna.night.3.notes: The pause makes the joke; slightly eerie, slightly wicked.

bark.wenna.night.4.notes: Very rude, very pleased with herself. The jab lands on 'idiots'.

bark.tam.1.notes: Said to anyone passing, the same fact again, a little louder each time.

bark.tam.2.notes: Repeating Pa like a lesson; slightly bored.

bark.tam.3.notes: 'The Watch laughed' is a child's grievance; flat with hurt, never sarcastic.

bark.brannoc.1.notes: A trade maxim over the anvil; a little dry. Balance the two halves like scales.

bark.brannoc.2.notes: Barely looks up; a warning that's also mild care. Two words, no lift.

bark.brannoc.3.notes: The nearest he comes to selling. Plain, a hint of pride on 'worth wearing'.

bark.brannoc.4.wants: to show off the weight of good iron
bark.brannoc.4.notes: A dry joke he doesn't smile at. Lean on 'stays hit' like the hammer landing.

bark.brannoc.night.1.notes: Not unkind; just the hour. Low and drowsy.

bark.brannoc.night.2.notes: Talking about his arm the way others talk about weather; 'old iron' is him. A low, private grumble.

bark.brannoc.night.3.notes: The fire is all he has with Nell gone; he doesn't know he's saying it. Quiet, almost tender; no self-pity.

bark.brannoc.night.5.wants: to keep the last two irons from anyone
bark.brannoc.night.5.notes: He's watching the rack at night for the buyer. Quiet threat in a tired voice; firm on 'Leave them'.

bark.vonnra.1.wants: to restate the terms to whoever passes
bark.vonnra.1.notes: Said to the air, as a rule of nature.

bark.vonnra.2.wants: to keep strangers at their proper distance
bark.vonnra.2.notes: A recited creed. Faint amusement at the predictability of those who will ask anyway.

bark.vonnra.3.wants: to keep the arrangement in everyone's ears
bark.vonnra.3.notes: Neither greedy nor warm; the way a clock says the hour.

bark.vonnra.night.1.wants: to show she is always keeping watch
bark.vonnra.night.1.notes: She does not sleep because she is waiting on the ford. Plain statement, a breath of weariness underneath.

bark.vonnra.night.2.wants: to remind herself what the night buys
bark.vonnra.night.2.notes: Bone-dry; she has done business with the dark and knows it.

bark.vonnra.night.3.wants: to keep the terms whatever the hour
bark.vonnra.night.3.notes: Low and steady. The 'even now' is tired and unyielding.

bark.vonnra.night.4.wants: to keep watch on what she set going
bark.vonnra.night.4.notes: She is looking south toward the crossing. The second sentence is certainty, not fear.

bark.keegan.1.notes: Clear command, with a hopeful lift on 'Not yet'.

bark.keegan.2.notes: Lecturer's gravity; she believes it and is a little proud of the phrasing.

bark.keegan.3.notes: Rehearsed retort, said to nobody, as if continuing an argument from earlier.

bark.keegan.night.1.wants: to remind herself why she is still awake

bark.keegan.night.2.notes: Alert, then deflating into a doubtful 'Probably'. A little jumpier than she would admit.

bark.keegan.night.3.notes: Correct and civil; the 'please' is policy, not nerves.

bark.keegan.night.4.wants: to convince herself she is not afraid
bark.keegan.night.4.notes: Pompous diction covering real fear of the dark. 'Very closely' gets a nervous emphasis.

bark.sella.1.notes: Cheerful hustle; the second half is friendly, not hurt.

bark.sella.night.1.notes: Plain and warm, a working line; not breathy.

bark.sella.night.2.notes: A friendly tip; the amusement is in what she leaves out.

bark.sella.night.3.notes: Bright and knowing; she enjoys her own sign.

bark.redcowl.2.notes: Matter-of-fact; a creed, not an excuse.

bark.redcowl.3.wants: to remind everyone who's in charge
bark.redcowl.3.notes: Almost cheerful, then 'Your choice' drops cold.

bark.redcowl.4.wants: to make a story of a threat
bark.redcowl.4.notes: Told like a joke with a chuckle at 'let the horse decide'; under it, nobody is sure it isn't true.

bark.jory.1.wants: to say it out loud and be rid of it
bark.jory.1.notes: Muttered, not for anyone; matter-of-fact on the surface, a shiver under it.

bark.jory.2.notes: Seventeen and mortified, but he doesn't mind really; 'It's a lot' is fond.

bark.jory.3.pace: flat statement, then a stark single word
bark.jory.3.wants: to not have seen what he saw
bark.jory.3.notes: 'Was.' is the whole line: someone in it died. Pause before it; say it flat and quiet.

bark.wayfinder.1.notes: Market-stall call; a darker, quieter twist on 'on purpose'.

bark.wayfinder.2.pace: brisk, a pause before 'Not always all of them'
bark.wayfinder.2.notes: Gallows humour delivered as a selling point.

bark.wayfinder.3.wants: to make sure buyers read the fine print
bark.wayfinder.3.notes: A pedant's insistence; 'not decoration' a little sharp.

bark.wayfinder.4.wants: to tell the half-hour rule as a warning
bark.wayfinder.4.notes: Said lightly, like weather. The 'thing' is spoken of with familiarity, not dread.

bark.wayfinder.night.1.notes: Quiet aside. The blood line is plain fact with a dry smile behind it.

bark.wayfinder.night.2.wants: to make light of the late hour
bark.wayfinder.night.2.notes: Night trade; a small, weary joke.

bark.guard.1.notes: Bored gate voice; the second sentence a dry observation, not a threat.

bark.guard.2.notes: Said a hundred times today; flat, not stern.

bark.guard.3.wants: to point the way and warn
bark.guard.3.notes: Two fragments, tossed off without looking up.

folk.1.notes: A nod in a word, barely looking.

folk.2.wants: to get you out of the way
folk.2.notes: Tossed over the shoulder while hauling.

folk.3.wants: to share the outrage of prices
folk.3.notes: Gossip-grumble; the second 'Two!' rises in disbelief.

folk.5.notes: Small talk, mildly pleased with the knee's wisdom.

folk.6.wants: to mark you as an outsider
folk.6.notes: A plain observation with an edge; not hostile.

folk.7.notes: Half to themself, tired of it.

folk.8.wants: to keep the queue in order

folk.9.notes: A glance and a wince; cuts themself off.

folk.10.wants: to share a joke about the priest
folk.10.notes: Gossip with a chuckle under it.

folk.13.wants: to warn you off the night

folk.15.notes: A jump, then flat disappointment on 'You.'

folk.16.notes: A grumble list; 'Morning.' tacked on deadpan.

folk.17.notes: Three muttered curses in a row, mounting a little.

folk.18.notes: Bawdy gossip, said low with a smirk.

folk.20.notes: Friendly dig, a smile in it.

folk.21.wants: to joke about a bad marriage
folk.21.notes: Dry, a little sad under it; deadpan last clause.

folk.23.notes: Bawdy wink in the voice, low.

folk.25.notes: Dry and tired; 'Says so himself.' almost fond.

folk.26.wants: to pass on the funeral news

folk.28.notes: Matter-of-fact; 'No offence' perfunctory, the last line darker.

folk.32.notes: Gossip with a squeak of disbelief on 'In daylight!'

folk.39.notes: Hushed; the Maeca bit convinced despite themself.

folk.41.notes: Fond eye-roll at Tam; 'but still' softer.

folk.42.notes: Gossip relish, each word set apart, deadpan.

folk.43.notes: Sardonic; 'Check your purse.' a quick aside.

folk.44.wants: to let you know they know

folk.45.notes: Quiet and certain; a little satisfied.

folk.50.notes: Quiet; the shutters line said low.

folk.51.notes: Disgusted; 'I bought eggs from that man' petty and real.

folk.61.wants: to ask if it was real
folk.61.notes: Quiet, unsettled; the image said slowly.

folk.66.wants: to know if you're a knight

folk.79.notes: Joking; 'Have you SEEN' with mock horror.

folk.80.notes: Whispered, louder on the second DON'T.

folk.82.wants: to let you know how things stand
folk.82.notes: Dry; the second clause a little worried.

folk.83.notes: Surprised, then warmly pleased; repeat softer.

folk.87.notes: Low, plain; the last line quiet.

folk.92.wants: to joke at their own expense

folk.96.notes: Each word set apart; amused suspicion at the end.

prologue.say.1.pace: slow, three pauses for the belt-book
prologue.say.1.wants: to let the dead man's last notes chill the player
prologue.say.1.notes: Say the eyes plainly. Read each belt-book line a touch flatter and thinner, the hand worsening; the singing line last and quietest.

prologue.say.2.wants: to pass on a dead man's warning
prologue.say.2.notes: Narration part low and still; the jaw's words dry, hoarse, almost a whisper, two short orders. No ghostly effects in the reading.

prologue.say.3.wants: to make the dark feel near
prologue.say.3.notes: Two plain sentences; the second a little lower.

prologue.say.4.wants: to give a breath and point the way
prologue.say.4.notes: A held beat after 'For now.' Then the road, plainly, a little lighter.

prologue.say.5.wants: to let the horror sit in plain words
prologue.say.5.notes: Image by image; do not lean on 'They were waiting.', just say it and stop.

prologue.say.6.wants: to put the player on guard
prologue.say.6.notes: Plain. 'It turns to look at you.' close and quiet, not dramatic.

prologue.say.7.pace: slow, a pause before the girl
prologue.say.7.wants: to make the player see who they killed
prologue.say.7.notes: Fight's end said plainly; then a breath, and the girl in a low, level voice. The new boots last, very quiet.

prologue.say.8.wants: to draw the player on toward the ford
prologue.say.8.notes: Quiet after the fight; 'a cold blue light' soft, a little far off.

prologue.say.9.wants: to make the strange feel almost homely
prologue.say.9.notes: Plain; the faintest dryness on 'The graves are listening.' No spook.

prologue.say.10.wants: to show the Warden before it moves
prologue.say.10.notes: Low, unhurried; the lamp in its fist is the last image, held.

prologue.say.11.wants: to let the heart draw the eye
prologue.say.11.notes: Plain description; 'full of cold light' slightly softer.

prologue.say.12.wants: to let dawn come after the long night
prologue.say.12.notes: A little warmth for the first time; 'Grey light, then gold.' slow.

prologue.say.13.wants: to tell the player what they are, and what it costs
prologue.say.13.notes: Plain and low, the rules said as fact. A real pause before the mother's face; say that last sentence gently and leave it.

prologue.say.14.wants: to warn the player the night is not over
prologue.say.14.notes: Soft first sentence; 'the ground is moving' plain and close.

prologue.say.15.wants: to tell the player they have risen again
prologue.say.15.notes: One line, low, almost a hand on the shoulder. No menace.

prologue.bark.1.wants: to raise the drowned to fight
prologue.bark.1.notes: A vast, hollow command from under water and iron; every word separate. Not a shout of anger: a rite.

prologue.bark.2.notes: Huge, cold, final, as if said a thousand nights; no emotion but duty.

prologue.bark.3.wants: to grab the heart before anyone can stop him
prologue.bark.3.notes: Oily and gleeful, a cackle on 'Oho!'; 'Nobody's!' the second time is a crow of triumph. Cave reverb.

prologue.bark.4.wants: to mock the survivor as he makes off
prologue.bark.4.notes: Low and smug, 'surface-meat' savoured; the thanks is a sneer, cackle trailing off.

waystation.say.1.wants: to give a small human trace
waystation.say.1.notes: Light and plain; the initials said as found, no sentiment.

waystation.say.2.1.notes: A touch of relish on 'turns sweetly'; the ledger line dry.

waystation.say.2.2.notes: Plain; the lock giving is small and physical. Dry on 'should have burned'.

waystation.say.3.wants: to plant the note as something that matters
waystation.say.3.notes: List the finds plainly; slow for the note, said in a quieter, older register.

waystation.say.4.wants: to bring the player into town and its eyes
waystation.say.4.notes: Three things, plainly; a slight dryness on 'News travels fast here.'

waystation.say.5.notes: Light and informative; 'maps to places the road forgets' a shade softer.

bark.stall.produce.1.notes: Market call, projected a little; 'crisp as frost' with a seller's lilt.

bark.stall.produce.2.notes: A list rattled off; 'the last of the beans' slightly mournful.

bark.stall.produce.3.wants: to make a bargain sound like a sacrifice
bark.stall.produce.3.notes: Old trader's joke, heard it a thousand times; theatrical sigh on 'robbing myself'.

bark.stall.cloth.2.wants: to land a sale with a dig

bark.stall.cloth.3.notes: Called out cheerfully, a local's pride.

bark.stall.herbs.1.notes: Rattled names, a pitch learned by heart.

bark.stall.herbs.2.notes: A little rivalry; half to themself.

bark.stall.herbs.3.notes: Matter-of-fact; the second sentence a resigned shrug.

bark.stall.pots.1.notes: Loud and cheery; the last phrase a self-mocking joke.

bark.stall.pots.2.wants: to show the pot rings true
bark.stall.pots.2.notes: As if knocking a pot; 'Hear that?' pleased.

bark.stall.pots.3.notes: Sizing you up with a grin; deadpan.

verge.say.1.wants: to let the player feel the truce
verge.say.1.notes: Quiet; no relief pushed into it.

verge.say.2.wants: to warn the player their cloak has betrayed them
verge.say.2.notes: Brisk and close; 'on its feet' lands hard but not shouted.

verge.say.3.wants: to tell the player the wolves know what they've done
verge.say.3.notes: Clipped; the Maeca clause said as a reminder, plain.

verge.say.4.wants: to raise the hair on the player's neck
verge.say.4.notes: Low, under the breath. One line, stop.

verge.say.5.wants: to show the camp accepts the player
verge.say.5.notes: Unbothered; 'go back to their dice' almost bored.

verge.say.6.wants: to let the thing in the pit unsettle
verge.say.6.notes: Plain description; set 'probably' apart with small pauses, and do not quite believe it.

verge.say.7.wants: to let the player hear the Morrow pray
verge.say.7.notes: Barely above a whisper. Give each fragment space; 'Praying.' last and quiet, the plainest word in it.

verge.say.8.wants: to point the player at the truth
verge.say.8.notes: Plain; the second sentence dry and level, the clue, not a joke.

verge.say.9.notes: Read like a search, item by item; slight weight on 'torn manifest'.

verge.say.10.notes: Tracker's plainness; 'Toward the ravine.' slightly lower.

verge.say.11.wants: to give the player a rest
verge.say.11.notes: Warm and quiet, like sitting down.

verge.say.12.1.notes: List the signs flat; the last sentence plain, the horror in the words, not the voice.

verge.say.12.2.notes: Short and plain; a slight hush on 'milky'.

verge.say.13.wants: to connect the water to the chapel without saying so
verge.say.13.notes: Plain; let 'smells like a chapel lamp' land as an odd, small fact.

verge.say.14.wants: to show the source of the poison
verge.say.14.notes: Plain description; the prints and drag-marks said as clues.

verge.say.17.notes: Quick and tight but not shouted; 'Run.' one hard word.

verge.say.18.1.wants: to make the door feel alive
verge.say.18.1.notes: Measured; the eye image soft, 'The door is listening.' low and close.

verge.say.18.2.wants: to hint the door wants the dark

verge.say.19.1.wants: to let the old inscription chill
verge.say.19.1.notes: Read the inscription in a slightly more formal, carved register; the empty notches plain.

verge.say.19.2.notes: Plain; 'hums against your teeth' close and quiet.

verge.say.20.wants: to show the player the key

verge.say.21.wants: to give the bones their one sentence
verge.say.21.notes: Narration plain and slow; the skull's words thin, dry, close, almost no voice.

verge.say.22.wants: to let the one-way prints frighten
verge.say.22.notes: Plain; small beat on 'None coming away.' The token said as a clue, evenly.

verge.say.23.wants: to make the find feel sacred
verge.say.23.notes: Soft; the first clause gentle, the circlet clear and cold.

verge.cagelines.1.wants: to show what the cages did
verge.cagelines.1.notes: Plain; the nails line quiet and level.

verge.cagelines.2.wants: to let gratitude be almost too much
verge.cagelines.2.notes: One plain line, a touch weary, kind.

verge.cagelines.3.wants: to let Jory's fear for his uncle break through
verge.cagelines.3.notes: Narration short; Jory's words given as quoted, quieter and broken off at each dash, not acted out.

verge.say.25.notes: Plain; 'like a bone' unemphasised. The last two stops get slower.

verge.say.26.wants: to let the cost of the blast be seen
verge.say.26.notes: No relish, no pity in the voice; image after image, the last sentence quietest.

verge.say.27.wants: to make the player sit with the burning
verge.say.27.notes: Said plainly and low; do not perform the screaming. A pause before 'and then there is only the fire.'

verge.say.28.1.wants: to open a way into something strange
verge.say.28.1.notes: Quick first clause; softer for the glade.

verge.say.28.2.wants: to open a way into something strange
verge.say.28.2.notes: Workmanlike first clause; softer for the glade.

verge.say.29.wants: to show the Pack has come
verge.say.29.notes: Plain and calm; let it feel like company, not triumph.

verge.say.30.wants: to give the player back their things after death
verge.say.30.notes: Low and kind, a shade dry on 'most of them'.

verge.bark.1.notes: Yelled over combat; pitched up, tinny ring on 'OI!'. Small and fierce.

chapter.1.wants: to remind the player time is short
chapter.1.notes: Plain; 'The clock is running.' flat and firm.

chapter.2.wants: to give the rescue its due

chapter.3.wants: to weigh a rescue against a fire
chapter.3.notes: Warm first sentence; the second plain and lower.

chapter.4.wants: to hint the cargo will matter
chapter.4.notes: Warm first; dry, almost amused on 'another story'.

chapter.5.notes: Plain; second sentence quieter, no catch in the voice.

chapter.6.wants: to hold the player to account
chapter.6.notes: Level; no blame in the tone, the facts do it.

chapter.7.notes: One plain line, low. Leave silence after.

chapter.8.wants: to give the player a little credit
chapter.8.notes: A trace of a smile; still plain.

chapter.9.notes: Three words. Say them and stop.

chapter.11.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.11.notes: An epithet, as in an old tale; read just the 'say' phrase, low and plain.

chapter.13.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.13.notes: An epithet with a sting; plain, slight weight on 'ledger'.

chapter.14.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.14.notes: Plain; let 'sold' carry it, no scorn added.

chapter.15.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.15.notes: Plain and level, as a ledger would put it.

chapter.16.wants: to name the player by their deeds

chapter.17.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.17.notes: The kindest of the epithets; warm, still plain.

chapter.18.wants: to name the player by their deeds

chapter.19.wants: to name the player by their deeds

chapter.20.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.20.notes: Flat; the name a town would mutter.

chapter.21.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.21.notes: Low and close, a winter's-tale cadence; the truest of the names.

chapter.22.wants: to name the player by their deeds
chapter.22.notes: Plain, with the faintest elegy in 'late of'.

chapter.beasts.slaughtered.notes: Plain first two; a pause, then 'It is also very quiet.' quieter.

chapter.beasts.allied.wants: to mark the alliance and its cost
chapter.beasts.allied.notes: Plain; dry on the second sentence.

chapter.beasts.cured.wants: to give the player a clean ending
chapter.beasts.cured.notes: Warm and even, the easiest breath in the game.

chapter.beasts.exploited.wants: to let the player hear what people say
chapter.beasts.exploited.notes: Level; 'People talk, in the end.' slightly lower, no lecture.

chapter.beasts.ignored.wants: to make neglect feel like a choice
chapter.beasts.ignored.notes: Plain; the second sentence closer and colder.

chapter.caravan.returned.notes: Plain, a little warmth at the end.

chapter.caravan.kept.wants: to remind the player they're known

chapter.caravan.with_kerchiefs.notes: Plain, a little shrug in it.

vonnra.f_ember.3.pace: very slow, a held beat before 'approve'
vonnra.f_ember.3.wants: to let the survivor feel watched, and graded
vonnra.f_ember.3.notes: The only praise in her fortune, and it is for waste: something nobody will ever buy. 'Approve' set down like a coin on the table. No warmth; no contractions.

vonnra.f_ember.5.wants: to show she knows who bought the crates without saying it
vonnra.f_ember.5.notes: Read the cargo's road like a ledger entry. 'I think you know who that was' is not a question: leave it lying there.

snib.first.1.wants: to stop you without having to fight you
snib.first.1.notes: Starts at a shout and loses it by 'Snib is the foreman'. 'Snib does not know who' is a lie told to the culprit's face; 'Snib knows exactly who' blurts out a beat later. 'Quick.' is pleading.

snib.hub.1.wants: to make you feel guilty about the pump
snib.hub.1.notes: The broken pump again, with a long-suffering lean on BROKEN; the contradiction lands as before. 'Foreman is still foreman' is his last scrap of dignity.

snib.hub.2.wants: to sound in charge of a change he fears
snib.hub.2.notes: 'Boss likes deeper' is brave; 'Boss has not SAID he likes it' is the panic underneath. Settle back into 'Foreman is still foreman' as reassurance to himself.

verge.say.15.wants: to make the player feel one charge's weight in the hand
verge.say.15.notes: Low and close, as if not to wake them. A small pause before 'the way they have waited for everyone': the crates are patient, and that is the threat.

verge.say.16.wants: to let the relief arrive in the silence
verge.say.16.notes: 'One at a time' is a held breath; 'not go off' lands flat and quiet, almost dry. No triumph.

chapter.12.wants: to name the survivor by the one brave thing
chapter.12.notes: An epithet on the chapter's last page; the name before it is not recorded, so start as if it has just been said.
